newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds end weaker, hurt by drop in dollar.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds end weaker, hurt by drop in dollar.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed weaker in active trade on Thursday, with a sharp drop in the value of the Canadian dollar and weaker U.S. Treasuries hurting prices, analysts said.

"It was dollar story really. There were some minor losses in North American bonds as a result of the Philadelphia Fed (index report), but the big story was the currency and the meltdown at the short end of the curve," said Andrew Pyle, head of fixed income research with ABN AMRO Bank Canada.
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond rose C$0.22 to C$119.77 to yield 6.492 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond fell 4/32 to yield 6.49 percent. The bonds traded to yield at par, compared with a positive spread of one basis point at Wednesday's close.

Canadian bonds began the session stronger, reaching a record-low yield of 6.472 percent. A stronger than expected Philadelphia Fed survey later in the morning weighed on Canadian and U.S. bond prices.

But weakness in the Canadian currency had the biggest impact on fixed-income prices. Canada's dollar weakened to as low as C$1.3782 (US$0.7256) after the Bank of Canada failed to hike interest rates as some had expected.
Pyle said financial markets are now testing the Bank of Canada, trying to get it to raise rates by weakening the Canadian dollar. The move is taking its toll on short-term fixed-income securities.
"It was an ugly day on the short end of the curve," said ABN's Pyle.
Canada's three-month when-issued T-bill, a key indicator of the market's expectations about short-term rates, weakened to yield 3.35 percent from 3.25 percent at the close of trading on Thursday.

On the economic front, the Canadian consumer price index report for June today had no major impact on bond prices, dealers said. The report showed the so-called core CPI rose 0.2 percent on the month and 2.0 percent on the year.
In new issue news, the Government of Canada said on Thursday it planned to auction on July 23 C$1.3 billion of bonds with a coupon of 8 percent and maturing on June 1, 2027.

In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bond fell C$0.34 to C$109.59 to yield 5.948 percent. The U.S. 10-year bond fell 1/32 to yield 6.19 percent. The negative spread moved to 24 basis points from 28 basis points on Wednesday.
